content.text: The only parity language in the document runs in our favour, and no reverse obligation exists.

input.quote: TrueLink agrees that the costs for any Hosting Services will not increase for a period of one year from the date of this Agreement and that rates charged for Hosting Services will not exceed that charged by TrueLink to any other party.
input.rationale: The only most-favoured-nation language in the Agreement runs in our favour: in § 6 (DOCUMENTATION AND DISPUTES, p0047) TrueLink — the Vendor — undertakes that its Hosting Services rates "will not exceed that charged by TrueLink to any other party," plus a one-year price freeze. That is a Vendor-granted MFN benefiting Client, which the rule expressly welcomes and directs us not to redline. I checked the remainder of the document for a reverse-direction obligation: § 5 COMPENSATION (p0045) sets only Client's payment mechanics with no parity or price-matching covenant, and § 8 COVENANTS AND WARRANTIES OF CLIENT (p0051-p0058) contains no obligation for Client to extend TrueLink terms no less favourable than those given to third parties or to match third-party offers. Searches for "no less favorable", "most favored", and price-matching language returned no other hits. There is therefore no MFN burdening Customer, which meets the preferred position (no MFN obligation on Customer). No redline proposed. Noted only for the record: the Vendor MFN is limited to Hosting Services rates and has no audit or true-up mechanic to verify compliance, but that is an enhancement beyond this rule's scope rather than a deviation.
